brief: UBS's Global Economics & Markets Outlook 2027/2028 flags that consensus S&P 500 earnings growth of 17.8% in 2027 and 16.9% in 2028 is already a high bar. The key risk: forward earnings revisions start to roll over, since the market has historically struggled when 12- and 24-month forward earnings growth revisions turn negative, especially from expectations as elevated as today's. UBS notes this year began with 12-month forward growth expectations of 15.1% against likely realised growth of 34.7%, but says a repeat beat now depends unusually heavily on hyperscalers sustaining the AI infrastructure build-out. Valuations, by contrast, are becoming a potential source of support: in the US and EM, Tech and Semis have derated sharply despite strong earnings and account for nearly three-quarters of the market's derating. UBS reads this as scepticism about the sustainability of the investment boom's pace and magnitude, not evidence that fundamentals have deteriorated, citing cloud revenue growth annualizing near 100% in Q3, still-low enterprise AI adoption, and compute capacity still short of future demand. UBS's end-2027 S&P 500 target of 8,900 conservatively assumes no re-rating.
